The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`

No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. ## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `381d735b88f5b03f0fa3a32f8ec44258debea93a`
Local-runs: none

Inputs: card #21068 (body; triage 5925807861, claim 5925905189, os-dev-report 5927222135), PR #21123 (body, its 5 files, the net diff against `main` at merge-base `9c8b65aa2`: +552 / -34), and the 34 check-runs on the head. The head was re-read at this write and had not moved. Nothing was built, run or re-run locally.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **The accept-set change, named right.** `resolveFilterToken` / `resolveFilterTokens` (`packages/core/src/utils/filter-tokens.ts`) now refuse a date macro whose computed instant is an invalid `Date`. Before: a day-or-coarser macro spelled the text `Invalid Date` (compared as text; every row under `$lt`), and a sub-day one threw an uncoded `RangeError` from `toISOString` (REST answered 500 `INTERNAL_ERROR`). After: a coded 400 at every position the engine resolves. A narrowing; nothing new is accepted.
2. **Raised once, in core, before either spelling.** The diff lifts the instant out of its spelling: `dateMacroInstant` answers `{ at, spelled }` for the four fixed tokens, the period tokens and the parameterised grammar (`resolvePeriodToken` now returns the bounding `Date`), and the one guard, `Number.isNaN(macro.at.getTime())`, sits between the instant and `toISOString` / `asYmd`. `resolveFilterTokens` reaches it through `walk` → `resolveFilterToken`, so every caller inherits it. The objectql and rest diffs are tests only: no second validity or range copy outside core, and the engine's year-range judge (PR #21065) is untouched.
3. **The `Date`'s own validity, not a second year range.** The guard asks `getTime()` of the instant; `SUPPORTED_TEMPORAL_YEARS` is read for the message's prose only. The edge pins show it: `{273847_years_ago}` still resolves to `-271821-09-30` for the engine's judge, `{273848_years_ago}` is refused; the same on the `_from_now` side and at exactly -8.64e15 ms for minutes. I also read the arithmetic the guard depends on: `addUnits`, `addMonthsClamped` and `wallClockToUtcMs` (`setUTCFullYear` / `setUTCMinutes` on NaN parts) yield an invalid `Date` without throwing for every unit, so the guard is reached for years, months, weeks, days, hours and minutes alike; the core pin's eight tokens cover each.
4. **`judgeFilter` agrees with execution.** `judgeWhereAdmission` calls the same `resolveWhereFilterTokens`, and `admissionRefusalOf` turns any thrown `Error` carrying a string `code` and a numeric `status` into the verdict, so the module-private class qualifies without being named. Pinned in the objectql suite: `{ ok: false, code: 'INVALID_FILTER', status: 400, message }` with the message equal to execution's, on both card rows.
5. **The code: `INVALID_FILTER`, judged against each declared meaning.** `FILTER_TOKEN_UNRESOLVED` is declared, everywhere it is stated, as a context the request does not carry: the class docblock ("the spelling is correct, the context is not"), spec `EngineFilterJudgementOptions.context` ("A placeholder whose value this context does not carry is REFUSED"), engine.ts's stage-2 comment, and the published core / objectql / spec CHANGELOG entries (`{current_user_id}` with no user, `{record_id}`). Here the context is complete, and the author's fix is a smaller offset: that code reads false. `FILTER_TOKEN_UNKNOWN` is declared as outside the vocabulary, and `classifyFilterToken` vouches for this token: false. `INVALID_FILTER` is the spec catalog's standard member (`errors.zod.ts`: "Invalid filter expression") and the code this family already answers for a resolved macro outside its column's years (#20844) and for a literal of the same value (#20264): true, and one code across the whole offset axis. The card's scope and triage's direction left the choice to measurement; the measurement is right, and no code was minted.
6. **Public surface.** `DateMacroPastDateRangeError` is declared without `export`; core's `index.ts` re-exports `filter-tokens.js` with `export *`, which carries exported bindings only, and no other file names the class, so it is absent from the CJS and ESM entries by construction (the dev's narrowed probe says the same). `resolvePeriodToken`'s return-type change is module-private. `resolveFilterToken` / `resolveFilterTokens` keep their signatures. The refusal carries `code`, `status` and `token`.
7. **Doors downstream.** REST reads a thrown error's numeric `status` and string `code` generically, so the SQLite door answers 400 `INVALID_FILTER` without naming the class; pinned at `where`, the per-aggregation `filter` and `having`, with no read of the object. The core-internal caller `analytics-date-range.ts` resolves preset tokens only (`today`, `week_start`, `30_days_ago` and their kin), none of which can land past the range. service-analytics' three callers now receive the coded error in place of the text or the `RangeError`; the dev says so and did not measure those doors end to end. A narrowing in the right direction, outside this card's surface.
8. **Pins match the direction.** Both card rows on the memory cell (objectql's recording driver: the refusal lands before any driver read, the construction PR #21065 used and the claim admitted as "a sibling") and on SQLite (REST over `SqlDriver`, the card's two rows), each beside an in-range control (`{100_years_ago}`, `{1_hour_ago}`). `Invalid Date` and `Invalid time value` are asserted absent from every message and body.
9. **Docs.** No hand-written page under `content/docs` names this family's refusal (nothing matches `years_from_now` or "outside its column's years"); the drift bot's five pages are reached through the `INVALID_FILTER` literal alone, and PR #21065 touched no docs either. Nothing is stale, and `content/docs/releases/` is untouched, as the guardrail requires.

Observation, not a defect: for the fixed token `now`, a caller-supplied invalid `ctx.now` is now refused by the same class (whose message speaks of an offset); before, it threw the uncoded `RangeError`. Not an authorable input.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset `.changeset/21068-macro-past-date-range.md`: `@objectstack/core: minor`, headed `fix(core)!:`, `**BREAKING**`, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, exactly one ADR-0087 marker, `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`. It matches what the diff publishes: core's two exported resolvers narrow their accept set, and no export, published type or authorable key moves. AGENTS.md: `(narrowing)` is BREAKING and ships as `minor` under the launch-window convention, the precedent of `dcd3309f2` (#20844) and core's `89f87f2` / `3062e50` entries. Not `skip-changeset`: core publishes.
- Only `@objectstack/core` carries code; objectql and rest gain tests. The changeset names the engine positions and the REST door whose answers change through core, and the config's `fixed` group bumps them in step.
- The marker's category fits the facts read here: no ADR-0087 id covers a value range or a resolved value, the class is not exported, the vocabulary is unchanged, and the body states what is refused and what an author sees. `Check Changeset` and `Lint & Repo Gates` are success on the head.
- `Clause-②:` line: `no (narrowing)` in the PR body and in the changeset, the declaration the claim prescribed. A query answered 200 with every row, or an uncoded 500, is now a coded 400; nothing new is accepted.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: none.
- Dev flag 1 (authoring accepts any `N` in `{N_unit_ago}`; such a stored filter is refused at run time only): true. `os validate` and lint's `validate-filter-tokens` are outside this card's file surface, and the family's year-range offsets (`{8000_years_from_now}`) were left the same way by #21065. Answered: a note, not a condition of this PR; the lint owner may card it if a producer ever writes such an offset.
- Dev flag 2 (engine.ts `resolveWhereFilterTokens` and spec `EngineFilterJudgementOptions.context` doc comments name only the two `FILTER_TOKEN_*` codes): read; both remain true, and the spec one would need `packages/spec` artifact regeneration to touch. Answered: polish, outside the surface, not a condition.
- NOT MEASURED locally (`check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, `check:type-check-debt`): answered by the head's check-runs. `Build Core`, `Type Check · debt ledger`, `Type Check · workspace`, `Type Check · consumer gates` and `Lint & Repo Gates` are success.
- Check-runs on the head, read at this write: 34 in all, 31 `success` (Test Core 1 to 6 and its rollup, TypeScript Type Check, Build Core, Dogfood Regression Gate 1 to 3, Dogfood Verify CLI, Temporal Conformance on live PG + MySQL, Lint & Repo Gates, the four Type Check jobs, Check Changeset, Check PR Size, Auto Label, Check Documentation Links, Flag docs affected by code changes, Governed Surface Queue Guard, `filter`, and the four claim / single-writer / part-of guards), 3 `skipped` by path filter or opt-in (Build Docs, Console Pin Gate, Packed-tarball smoke), none `in_progress`. The one pending item is the Vercel commit status, which is not a check-run and not a gate.
- Memory cell: a recording driver rather than `InMemoryDriver`, the construction the claim admitted and #21065's precedent; the InMemoryDriver readings sit in the PR body's probe table. Accepted.
